coverage: Thursday 27 Aug 2026 pre-Asia-open run (~07:02-08:20 SGT). Latest completed session is Wednesday 26 Aug for the US (S&P ~7,676, Nasdaq 26,130, VIX 15.21, -1.55%); HK/SG/JP/KR's own daily bars had not yet consolidated past Tuesday 25 Aug at spine-fetch time (Asian bars lag). Nvidia's FQ2 print landed after Wednesday's US close, the dominant overnight story. SGX opens 09:00 SGT and HKEX 09:30 SGT, both after this run.
tldr: Nvidia crushed FQ2 (revenue $96.2B +106% y/y, FQ3 guide $108B vs $104.2B consensus, shares +14.5% after-hours) -- the cleanest confirmation yet the AI-capex cycle is intact, resolving last quarter's three-way whale split (Tepper/Loeb/Soros) in the bulls' favor.

Core PCE held in-line but sticky at 3.3% y/y and GDP confirmed at 1.5% -- neither derails nor confirms a September Fed cut; Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote (Friday 28 Aug) is now the dominant near-term catalyst after he explicitly left a 2026 hike on the table.

Gold/silver ETFs and miners pulled back Wednesday (GLD -1.58%, SLV -1.17%, GDX -2.94%) even as futures held firm (GC=F +0.50%, SI=F +0.14%) -- an ETF/futures timing divergence coinciding with the hot-but-in-line PCE print; silver still capped its best month in years (~+17-18% in August).

Trump renewed the push to fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook (response deadline was today) and the 30-year Treasury sits at a 22-year price low (yield >5.33%) -- both a structural tailwind for holding the gold/silver hedge independent of today's data.

Iran and Oman continued talks toward a temporary Hormuz shipping corridor, pushing oil to a third straight down session (WTI -0.59%, Brent -2.24%) -- easing one input into the inflation narrative that's been supporting the metals trade.

Berkshire, Ackman, Druckenmiller and Tepper all made large, partially offsetting Q2-2026 13F moves (Berkshire's $21.1B GOOGL add; Ackman's new Visa/Mastercard/S&P Global stakes; Druckenmiller's 10x AMZN build funded by a full chip exit; Tepper's 12-name narrowing) -- no new activist filings surfaced this week.

regime.label: Cautiously risk-on but fragile: NVDA beat-and-raise offsets a hot-but-in-line PCE, with Warsh's Jackson Hole debut the last binary catalyst before September FOMC
regime.oneLiner: A genuinely constructive tape (AI capex intact, inflation not re-accelerating, calm VIX, tight credit spreads) is capped by real uncertainty over Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish-leaning Friday speech and a historic long-bond selloff reflecting fiscal stress independent of the Fed.
